checks.label: permutation-thinned-chains
checks.title: Permutation null on thinned chains
supports: the null sides at the effective sample size
checks.setup: Zoo chains {py:func}`~mixed_signals.zoo.cases.ar1_chains` with the coefficients 0.9 and 0.5, 32 walkers and 100 times the true autocorrelation time τ in steps, reduced by {py:func}`~mixed_signals.mcmc.reduce.reduce_chains` (thinning by the autocorrelation time). Each of the 300 replicates at coefficient 0.9 and the 120 at 0.5 compares two independent runs, with the statistics of the first parameter and 99 permutation draws. The default null gives each side the effective sample size of its set, through the arguments `first_n_eff` and `second_n_eff` of {py:func}`~mixed_signals.nulls.permutation.permutation_null`; the contrast permutes all samples with sides of the sample count. The thinned samples keep some autocorrelation, so a null of full sides is too narrow. The reduction estimates the autocorrelation time left after thinning at 1.3686 ± 0.0015, against 1.4292 ± 0.0014 that the thinning factor implies for an AR(1) chain, (1 + φᵏ)/(1 − φᵏ). Sides of N/τₖ samples therefore make the default null narrower than the scatter of the mean shift by their ratio, 1.044 in variance; the replicates at coefficient 0.9 give 1.217 ± 0.100 for the default null and 1.69 ± 0.14 for the sides of N, against one for a null of the right width. The developers allow the rejection rate of the mean shift at coefficient 0.9, the slowest chain, up to 1.5 times the level, plus three binomial errors at that bound. At the 5% level that lets σ_sig read up to 10% high: a rate of 7.5% is the rate of a null 1.10 times too narrow in standard deviation. The reason is that the τₖ of the reduction reads low. The other claims of the check stay strict.

checks.label: tail-fit
checks.title: Tail fit of σ_sig on known nulls
checks.setup: 500 replicates of each case. The nulls have a known survival function: the standard normal, the chi-squared distribution with 1 and 4 degrees of freedom and the largest of 8 absolute standard normals, all drawn with `jax.random`, with the true p-value from `jax.scipy.special.ndtr` or `gammaincc`. The value of each case has the p-value of a normal at 3σ, 4σ and 5σ, and {py:func}`~mixed_signals.sigma.significance.null_significance` reads its σ_sig against 200 or 1 000 draws. The record in the zoo check of the module gives medians for a normal, a Kolmogorov and a chi-squared null with 4 degrees of freedom; this page reruns the normal and the chi-squared null of the record and not the Kolmogorov distribution. A claim lets the median of each of those two nulls lie within the range of the record plus half a unit of its last digit, plus the standard errors of the median, and a second claim lets the median at 3σ of all four nulls lie within 0.15 of the truth plus the standard errors. The standard error of a median is 1.25 times the half-width of the 16th to 84th percentile range over the square root of the replicates. The fit that the developers rejected, the unconstrained maximum likelihood fit of {cite:t}`knijnenburg2009fewer`, is not rerun here; its failure (a p-value of zero in 18 to 79% of the cases beyond 3σ) is in the record of the module. The fit that the package uses keeps the support above the value ({cite:t}`peschel2026permapprox`) and uses the estimator of {cite:t}`zhang2009new`. The record gives single values, 4.9 and 7.7, at 10σ and 100σ against 200 normal draws; the claim is that each lies between the 16th and 84th percentiles of the replicates.

checks.label: effect-recovery
checks.title: Recovery of known shifts
supports: the done criterion of session 12: σ_eff recovers the zoo's shifts
checks.setup: Shifted zoo Gaussians ({py:func}`~mixed_signals.zoo.cases.shifted_gaussians`, 4 parameters) with true shifts 0, 0.2, 0.5, 1, 2, 1 000 samples per set and 12 replicates per shift. Each row uses the default permutation null, then {py:func}`~mixed_signals.sigma.maps.null_subtract` and {py:func}`~mixed_signals.sigma.maps.sigma_eff` with the settings of the row. The marginal metrics read the first parameter, which carries the shift. The JS divergence and the Hellinger distance come from kernel estimates with the bandwidth factor of {py:func}`~mixed_signals.metrics.marginal.shared_bandwidth_factor`, and the Gaussian KL, W2 and Hellinger distance from the weighted moments. MMD squared takes the median bandwidth of the comparison, fixed once, and the Sinkhorn divergence takes ε at 0.25 times its square. Both sliced W2 estimators share 500 directions. The null has 99 draws for the cheap metrics, 49 for the kernel estimates, 30 for the empirical sliced W2 and 20 for the Sinkhorn divergence, fewer than the default 200. The marginal KS, W1 and AD also run at 10 000 samples per set with 5 replicates. The sample means of a replicate differ by a shift of their own, which scatters by about 0.045 at 1 000 samples, and every metric follows it, so a mean σ_eff compared with the true shift carries that scatter. A claim therefore tests the mean of the paired difference, σ_eff minus the sample shift of the same replicate, which has the same expectation as σ_eff minus the truth and a far smaller scatter. The tolerance is 3% of the true shift (6% for the KS statistic, which keeps a small positive bias), plus the standard errors of the paired differences. The zero shift has no claim here; the check {ref}`validation-signed-maps` covers it with 40 replicates.

checks.label: knn-ranks
checks.title: Ranks of the nearest-neighbour divergences
checks.setup: Unit Gaussians in 1, 4, 16 parameters, the second set shifted along one axis ({py:func}`~mixed_signals.zoo.cases.shifted_gaussians`), with 1 000 samples per set and 16 replicates per dimension and shift. The estimates are {py:func}`~mixed_signals.metrics.divergence.knn_kl_divergence`, {py:func}`~mixed_signals.metrics.divergence.knn_js_divergence` and {py:func}`~mixed_signals.metrics.divergence.knn_hellinger_distance` at the ranks 1, 3, 5, 10, against the permutation null with 14 draws, fewer than the default 200 and the 40 of the original check; every rank of a replicate uses the same sets and the same permutations. The resolution at the 1σ shift is the mean of (value minus null mean) over the root of the mean null variance of the replicates, because every replicate draws the same null again; it is read relative to k = 3. The Hellinger resolution is read in H² = sign(H)·H², the space in which the package subtracts the null of that metric. In H, where the null draws lie below zero, the slope of the signed root narrows the null spread against the signal, and the resolution reads high. At D = 16, the null draws of the Hellinger estimate H at k = 5 have the mean -0.166, and 224 of 224 of them lie below zero. The bias rows subtract the null mean as the σ_eff maps do, in squares for the Hellinger distance, and compare with the truth at the shift that the two sample sets hold, the difference of their means along the shifted axis, which has the same expectation as the true shift and a far smaller scatter. The default ranks are KL 3, JS 10, Hellinger 5. The record, at 3 000 and 10 000 samples, gave a resolution against k = 3 of 0.54 and 1.62 at k = 1 and 10 for KL, 0.58 and 1.87 for JS, and 0.17, 1.41 and 2.08 at k = 1, 5 and 10 for Hellinger; at the defaults JS lay within −1 to +3% of the truth up to D = 8, H² within 0 to −9%, and KL read −9 to −17% low at D = 4. The nearest-neighbour searches cost O(N²), and the JS estimate costs most, so this check runs at a smaller N and fewer replicates than the record. No estimate or null draw was NaN or infinite.

checks.label: ksg-bananas

checks.setup: The zoo's twisted Gaussian ({py:func}`~mixed_signals.zoo.cases.banana`, variance 100) at the twists 0.001, 0.002, 0.003, 0.01, 0.03, 0.1. The zoo does not tabulate its mutual information, so the script computes it. With t the twist times the variance, the second parameter is a unit normal plus t(z² − 1) for z standard normal, so the mutual information is the entropy of that sum minus ½ ln(2πe). Its density comes from composite 8-point Gauss-Legendre panels in z, with edges uniform in z² up to z = 7 and a shift of at most 0.2 along y per panel, and its entropy from the trapezoid rule with a step of 0.05; halving both changes every value by at most 9.6e-12 nats. The estimate is the KSG mutual information of {py:func}`~mixed_signals.diagnostics.dependence.dependence_statistics`, which returns it as an excess over the Gaussian value at the set's Pearson r; the table adds that value back. Sample counts 2 000, 1 000, 30 replicates per cell, ranks 10 (the default, which {py:data}`~mixed_signals.diagnostics.dependence.MUTUAL_INFORMATION_NEIGHBOURS` sets) and 3. The claims cover the bananas of twist at least 0.003, the faint one included, whose value of 0.0799 nats is the record's banana of 0.08 nats. Session 11 recorded k = 10 within −9 to +4% at 2 000 samples and −26% at 1 000 samples for the faint banana, and a resolution 1.7 times that of k = 3.

Each row calls the function of the package once as an engine would, after one call that compiles it, and reports the median of three calls, or the one call when it takes more than 10 s. Before a timer starts, all earlier work has finished, and the timer stops when the result is ready, because JAX dispatches asynchronously. The energy distance runs at 5 000, 10 000, 20 000 samples per set, which sets {py:data}`~mixed_signals._config.SAMPLE_CAP`, and the other comparison rows at 10 000; the sliced Sinkhorn divergence runs at 2 000 ({py:data}`~mixed_signals.metrics.ot.sliced.SLICED_SINKHORN_CAP`), and the dependence statistics at 2 000 ({py:data}`~mixed_signals.diagnostics.dependence.PAIR_CAP`), with the default directions of each sliced metric. In 16 dimensions the orthonormal bases round the number of directions asked for up to whole bases, so the rows state how many were asked for and how many the array holds. The record of 6.4 s for the sliced Sinkhorn divergence was measured with 20 independent directions. The median bandwidth and the calibration curve of the kNN KL map run once per comparison, so they have no extrapolation. The times depend on the machine in the stamp of this page; the record column holds the times that the sessions measured on an Apple M4 Pro CPU, 20 minutes for the dependence statistics of 201 sets being about 6 s per set.
